mbm-0543.clue: My whole garden grows on one green screen.
mbm-0543.quote: I wrote a program that sprouts one little leaf whenever I finish a page of homework. My brother found the key that makes it rain. By supper the ivy had reached the edge of the monitor.

mbm-0544.clue: My puppet's eyebrow is on a separate thread.
mbm-0544.quote: I fixed the thread to my little finger so the puppet can raise just one brow. The children shout the answer to his riddle before I even open his mouth. He's a terribly obvious detective.

mbm-0545.clue: My wake has its own seat at breakfast.
mbm-0545.quote: I skied across the lake before my father had finished his coffee. My friend took a picture of him on the dock with my reflection in the wake below his cup. Dad put it next to his cup at home.

mbm-0546.clue: I practice with my back to the mirror.
mbm-0546.quote: I used to watch myself through every form. My teacher covered the studio mirror with a sheet one Saturday. I could finally hear my feet land together. I face the plain wall for my first round now.

mbm-0547.clue: We hang a red ribbon where the wind can vote.
mbm-0547.quote: Our old beach net sags on one side. I tie a red ribbon to the middle and wait to see where it blows before I serve. When the loop hangs still the whole team goes quiet.

mbm-0548.clue: The tambourine has a borrowed uniform.
mbm-0548.quote: I broke one jingle in rehearsal. Our neighbor gave me two bottle caps from his soda counter. They make a little flat clatter right in the chorus, so the whole band calls that bit the soda solo.

mbm-0549.clue: My quilt has a piece of our hallway in it.
mbm-0549.quote: We tore out a worn runner when we moved. I saved a narrow strip of its pattern and sewed it across the foot of our quilt. On cold mornings my brother says the hallway has followed him into bed.

mbm-0550.clue: I can find the airport by its one blue door.
mbm-0550.quote: On my first skydive everything on the ground looked unfamiliar except the clubhouse's huge blue door. I drew it at the bottom of my logbook page. That tiny patch of paint felt like home from the sky.

mbm-0551.clue: We lend the island a tune.
mbm-0551.quote: My family canoes to a small island and everyone brings one line of a song. On the shore we put the lines together. Nobody agrees on how the last one goes, which is why we have to go back.

mbm-0552.clue: I got to paint the sound of a train.
mbm-0552.quote: For our play we needed an approaching train. I painted a row of tiny lit windows on a long roll and pulled it behind a cutout station wall. My sister shook a tin of washers for wheels.

mbm-0553.clue: My songbook has a patch of blue denim.
mbm-0553.quote: I stitched a cover for the little notebook I use at singing practice. There's a worn pale spot where my thumb holds the hard verse open. The rest of the book still has its original blue.

mbm-0554.clue: Our game ends at the blue fence.
mbm-0554.quote: I used to throw the frisbee too high. A neighbor painted a little cloud on the fence and told me to aim under it. I caught my first flat throw and my neighbor held up the paintbrush like a trophy.

mbm-0555.clue: One corner of my quilt comes from under the sink.
mbm-0555.quote: My granddad kept his oldest work shirt as a polishing rag. I washed a clean patch and put it beside the good cloth. When he saw the faded stripe he remembered the first cabinet he'd built.

mbm-0556.clue: I wear out my left shoelace first.
mbm-0556.quote: Every morning I reach the bakery as my friend opens the shutters. I turn left and run backward three steps so we can wave. My shoes bear the evidence even when the shutters open late.

mbm-0557.clue: Our high score is a two-person photograph.
mbm-0557.quote: The arcade machine forgot its scores each night. I held the camera while my cousin played, then we traded. In the reflection you can see us both trying very hard to look casual.

mbm-0558.clue: I know the tunnel by its note.
mbm-0558.quote: My putt went into a metal drainpipe on our homemade course and rang a low note all the way through. Dad cut two shorter pipes. We now come to hole nine to perform as well as putt.

mbm-0559.clue: The first person I bow to is in a photograph.
mbm-0559.quote: Our dojo has a faded group photo by the door. In the corner my teacher is a beginner with a crooked belt. I greet that kid on my way in, especially when my own belt won't sit straight.

mbm-0560.clue: I left the ground with a green button.
mbm-0560.quote: Before my jump my daughter tucked a green button in my logbook for luck. The landing field looked just as green beneath my open parachute. I painted four little buttonholes on the field in my sketch.

mbm-0561.clue: My shortest actor gets the loudest entrance.
mbm-0561.quote: I built a hand puppet no taller than a coffee mug. I hide it behind a huge painted door. When that door creaks open and the tiny emperor waves, the whole front row leans forward.

mbm-0562.clue: My partner leads the last three steps.
mbm-0562.quote: She taught me the waltz in her kitchen and kept one tiny turn for herself at the end. At a crowded dance I can feel that turn coming before the music gets there.

mbm-0563.clue: Our raft had a lunch bell.
mbm-0563.quote: I packed a metal camping cup on a carabiner. It rang against the lunch tin every time we hit a ripple. By the final bend we could all hear sandwiches coming.

mbm-0564.clue: My red skis are famous at the campsite.
mbm-0564.quote: I propped my water skis beside our tent while they dried. In the morning a spider had spun a perfect web between the tips. We ate breakfast watching dew shine on a very expensive clothesline.

mbm-0565.clue: I paint the part the tide took away.
mbm-0565.quote: I drew the rocks at low tide, left for lunch and came back to find my subject underwater. I finished the lower part of the canvas in green ripples. That afternoon is still coming in over half my painting.

mbm-0566.clue: I keep the clouds on tracing paper.
mbm-0566.quote: At the airfield I sketch each plane in my notebook, then add the weather on a separate thin sheet. Lift the gray cloud page and today's little trainer gets clear skies for as long as I like.

mbm-0567.clue: The crocodile has room for two fingers.
mbm-0567.quote: I crocheted a green finger puppet and made its snout far too long. My niece put another finger in the nose, and suddenly it could nod and argue. She made it head of the puppet show.
